newsitem.title: SPAIN: Rojo says rate fall speed in part from EMU outlook.
newsitem.headline: Rojo says rate fall speed in part from EMU outlook.

text.p: Bank of Spain Governor Luis Angel Rojo said on Wednesday that the speed of the fall in Spanish interest rates stemmed in part from market optimism on Spanish entry into the launch of Europe's single currency.
Rojo said the central bank must avoid rate cuts that promote excessive monetary growth.

On Tuesday, the Bank of Spain left its key money market rate unchanged at 5.25 percent, although many had expected it to shave the rate for the fifth time in 1997 given a sharp deceleration in inflation.
Long-term interest rates have dropped dramatically.

"...the general fall in assets and debt that we are experiencing now and which began some two years ago, wouldn't have been as far-reaching if it were not for the growing market conviction that Spain will enter into the (monetary) union from the first moment," Rojo said, speaking to a savings bank annual meeting.
He said the fall was appropriate but added that it should not prompt excessive monetary expansion.

"...This is a rational and likely movement which should be welcomed as long as two conditions are met. The first, whose responsibility lies with the monetary authority, would be to avoid excessive loan and monetary expansion from the fall," he said.
The second would be that financial institutions ensure that margins are sufficient to cover their costs.
